verses.1: And from the tent and its furnishings, as well as from the altar and its utensils, they made garments for the priest in the Holy Place. They also made the garments of the Holy Place that were meant for Aaron, just as Jehovah commanded Moses.
verses.2: And he made the earrings from gold. He also made a necklace and a bracelet.
verses.3: And they bent the golden sheets into shapes, so that they could be used within the framework and within the structure. They also used them within the second ring, and within the six elements that make up the entire structure.
verses.4: They made for him two pairs of bonds on both of his extremities.
verses.5: And he considered his own destruction to be a punishment for his actions. It was like the work of gold, silver, copper, and other metals being used to create weapons. It was also like the use of fire, as God commanded Moses to do.
verses.6: And they made the stones of the shrines from gold. The doors of these shrines were adorned with names of the Israelites.
verses.7: And he placed them on the shoulders of the Ark of the Covenant, as God commanded Moses.
verses.8: And he made the choker with careful craftsmanship, just like how gold is processed into jewelry. It consisted of a chain, a pendant, and six other decorations.
verses.9: It was quite long in both directions; its length and width were equal.
verses.10: And four tribes were filled with them: one tribe of Adam, and another tribe of Pithda. And the third tribe was Barakhet.
verses.11: And the second month went back to Sefir and Yahalom.
verses.12: And the third trumpet will be sounded, and it will bring about destruction and chaos.
verses.13: And the fourth throne is adorned with gold decorations, made of gold.
verses.14: And the stones with the names of the children of Israel are now twelve in number. Each stone bears the name of one person, for a total of twelve stones.
verses.15: And they made a necklace from gold wires. It was a beautiful piece of jewelry made of gold.
verses.16: And they made two golden candlesticks and two golden bowls. They placed the two bowls at both ends of the altar.
verses.17: And the two weights were placed on the two scales, at the ends of the rod.
verses.18: And the two ends of those straps were attached to the two poles. They were then placed on the shoulders of the Ephod, right in front of its face.
verses.19: And they made two golden plates, and they placed them on both ends of the altar, on its feet, which were located beyond the entrance to the temple.
verses.20: And they made two golden crowns, and they placed them on the two heads of the eagle. This was done so that the eagle could be adorned with these crowns from above its head.
verses.21: And they put the lampstand on its stand, with its branches tied together in a rope, so that it would remain stable on its stand. The lampstand was not to fall from its stand, as Jehovah commanded Moses.
verses.22: And he made the cover for the lamp, in a way that it could be used as a protective covering.
verses.23: And the covering that covers it is like a mouthpiece; around it, nothing can be taken away.
verses.24: And they made on the sides of the cover: ropes, hooks, and a second kind of fastening.
verses.25: And they made pure gold decorations, and they placed these decorations inside the frames, around the edges of the decorations.
verses.26: Phemon and Rimmon! Phemon and Rimmon! On the shoulders of those who serve God, as commanded by Jehovah to Moses.
verses.27: And they made the statutes that were six in number, as Ahron and his sons were commanded to make.
verses.28: And the branches of the vine, six in number; and the roots of the vines, six in number; and the entrances to the winepresses, six in number.
verses.29: And the altar, six cubits in length, with its base and frames, and its second panel – all these were made according to what Jehovah commanded Moses.
verses.30: And they made the sacred vessels of gold. They wrote on them the words of the Torah, which are sacred to Jehovah.
verses.31: And they set a pin on it, so that it could be placed on the tent from above, just as Jehovah commanded Moses.
verses.32: And all the work related to building the Tabernacle was completed. And the children of Israel did everything that Jehovah commanded Moses. So they did it.
verses.33: And they brought the tent to Moses. They brought along all its furnishings: the beams, the poles, and the stands.
verses.34: And the covering of the silent fields, and the covering of the trembling ones, and the cover of the darkness.
verses.35: The tent’s poles, and its boards, and the covering.
verses.36: Throw away all its contents, along with the bread that’s inside.
verses.37: They purified the holy lamp, along with its wicks and all its components. They also purified the oil used to light the lamp.
verses.38: And the golden altar, and the oil for the sacrifice, and the vessels used for sprinkling the blood, and the door of the sanctuary.
verses.39: I will destroy the idol of the Serpent, and also all its utensils and everything related to it. I will destroy the altar and all that belongs to it.
verses.40: They also repaired the doors and windows of the house, as well as its balconies. They also replaced the hinges and locks on all the doors and windows. In short, they repaired everything related to the house’s furnishings for the use of the guests.
verses.41: The garments of the priest shall be used for serving in the Holy Place. The garments of the Holy Place belong to Aaron, the priest, and also to his sons, who are also priests.
verses.42: Just as Jehovah commanded Moses, so did the children of Israel do all those tasks.
verses.43: And Moses saw all the work that had been done. He saw that they had done it as God had commanded. So, Moses blessed them.
